summary: A 1978 note on recent extensions to the SUPDUP protocol, describing changes made since the original specification. Its status is unknown.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 747 describes optional additions to SUPDUP negotiation. Terminals can report graphics abilities and input/output line speeds, and can request a character-mapping option for parentheses and square brackets.

questions: what are the new supdup negotiation variables
subtitle: Optional SUPDUP negotiation fields for graphics capabilities and terminal line speeds.

tldr.problem: SUPDUP was being extended, and user programs needed a way to report graphics capabilities and terminal line speeds during initial negotiation.
tldr.mechanism: The update adds the SMARTS, ISPEED and OSPEED negotiation variables and a TTYOPT bit, %TPPRN, for swapping parentheses and square brackets on input.
tldr.outcome: The RFC says the extensions are optional and upward and downward compatible, and that RFC 734 remains adequate for most SUPDUP programs.

today: The unit records RFC 747's status as Unknown. Its text describes optional additions to the SUPDUP protocol in RFC 734.

sections.title: Optional Additions to SUPDUP
sections.content:
RFC 747 describes changes to the SUPDUP protocol specified in RFC 734, including the graphics extension documented in RFC 746. The author says the extensions are optional and compatible with older and newer programs; RFC 734 remains an adequate description for most SUPDUP user and server programs.

The update adds three variables to initial negotiation, in the order SMARTS, ISPEED and OSPEED. The variable count is now -10,,0, or 777770000000 in octal.
sections.plainLanguage: The additions are optional, so programs can continue using the earlier SUPDUP description. Newer programs can send extra details during startup negotiation.

sections.title: SMARTS and Terminal Speeds
sections.content:
SMARTS describes terminal capabilities, especially graphics capabilities. If the graphics extension is not being used, SMARTS should be set to zero. RFC 746 describes the variable and graphics option in detail.

ISPEED and OSPEED report the terminal's input and output baud rates when known. A value of zero means the line speed is indeterminate. The RFC suggests sending these variables when the console line speed is known so the server can handle terminal buffering better.
sections.plainLanguage: SMARTS tells the server what the terminal can do. ISPEED and OSPEED tell it how fast input and output travel, or use zero when the speed is unknown.

sections.title: Parenthesis and Bracket Mapping
sections.content:
The RFC adds the %TPPRN TTYOPT bit, with value 0,,200. When enabled, the system swaps parentheses with square brackets on input.

The author notes that this can help LISP users whose terminal has parentheses as a shifted character but does not have square brackets. The bit is normally off, and servers are not required to implement it.
sections.plainLanguage: The optional bit swaps parentheses and square brackets as the user types. It is intended for terminals where square brackets are not directly available.

references.text: RFC 734, the SUPDUP protocol specification described as the starting point for these extensions.
Stallman, R., The SUPDUP Graphics Extension, RFC 746.
